Hand AI your product range, market and competitors and get a weekly log of who AI Mode cites.

Google put a new model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, into Search for everyone on 12 November. The model writing the answers has changed, so I'd treat that date as a new baseline for AI visibility. This clip covers the first two jobs I'd hand to AI to rebuild it.

First, give it your product range, market and main competitors. It writes twenty to thirty multi-part buyer questions, then runs each one in AI Mode every week and logs which brands and pages are cited.

Second, give it those questions and your sitemap. It lists the subtopics Google would likely search and marks which ones your site has no page for.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

Full episode and article at manual-focus.co.uk/blog/gemini-4-hydrogen-google-search-seo-teams/
clips.text: So what do you hand over? Get AI on this, first job. Rebuild your prompt set and check it every week. Give it your product range, your market and your main competitors, and it writes twenty to thirty multi-part buyer questions with budget, fit and use case in them. Then set it as a weekly routine, running each one in AI Mode from a UK location and logging which brands and pages are cited. Second, map the fan-out gaps. Give it those questions and your sitemap. It lists the subtopics Google would likely search for each one, and marks which have a page or clear section on your site and which have nothing.

Google's AI answers are built from subtopic searches, so every buyer question needs its own page or section.

Google put Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Search for everyone on 12 November and says it widens query fan-out, splitting one question into several smaller searches and linking to a broader range of sites. In this clip Hannah and I talk through what that means for a content team.

One long guide with the fit advice buried in paragraph nine gives Google less to cite than a page with a proper section on fit. Google also says it's showing more comparison tables, which fits the SISTRIX study we covered in October, where tables with a proper header row went with more AI citations.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

Full episode and article at manual-focus.co.uk/blog/gemini-4-hydrogen-google-search-seo-teams/
clips.text: So, the so what for a content team. If the answer is assembled from subtopics, a brand needs a page, or at least a clear section, for each one. That's the read. One long guide that buries fit advice in paragraph nine gives Google less to cite than a page with a proper section on fit. And Google says it's showing more comparison tables, which ties in with the SISTRIX study we covered in October, where tables with a proper header row went with more AI citations.
